title_en: Armed robberies on discounters and kiosks
description_en: On Saturday and Sunday, a discount store and a kiosk were robbed in Neustadt and Gröpelingen. The perpetrators fled with cash, and the police are looking for witnesses. Shortly before closing time, at around 9:35 PM on Saturday, a masked man entered the supermarket on Gröpelinger Heerstraße. He climbed onto the conveyor belt of a checkout and shouted that he wanted money. He then kicked an employee several times in the back, threatened him with a knife, and demanded that he open the till. After the 22-year-old opened the till, the robber took the money and then fled. The perpetrator is described as being approximately 1.85 meters tall and slim. He wore a black balaclava, black socks, dark grey shorts, an anthracite-colored hooded jacket, black gloves, and white Nike brand shoes with a black symbol. One day later, at around 9:40 PM, two men approached a kiosk on Pappelstraße. The duo threatened an employee with a knife and a blank-firing pistol, had the till opened, and grabbed several banknotes from it. They then fled in an unknown direction. The suspects are believed to be between 20 and 30 years old and between 1.70 and 1.80 meters tall. One wore a dark cap, a black sweater with a white emblem and white stripes on the arms, jeans, dark shoes, a black shoulder bag, and a dark cloth over his face. He also had a conspicuous ring on the middle finger of his right hand. His accomplice wore a black hooded jacket, black jogging pants, dark sneakers, and a light-colored cloth over his face.

Tomorrow, a demonstration by the "Fridays for Future" initiative will take place in Bremen. The organizers expect up to 1000 participants. The police will accompany the demonstration and expect traffic disruptions along the route. The registered event begins at 12 PM on the market square, after which the procession is expected to set in motion around 12:30 PM. The route runs from the Cathedral via Ostertorstraße towards Ostertorsteinweg, across the Sielwall intersection to the "Am Dobben" stop. Subsequently, participants will walk through An der Weide street towards the main train station, turn onto Herdentorsteinweg towards Herdentor, and return via Schüsselkorb and Violenstraße to the market square, where a final rally is planned. The Bremen Police will accompany the assemblies and ask all road users to be prepared for traffic disruptions along the procession routes. These areas should be avoided with vehicles if possible and widely bypassed.

title_en: SV Werder Bremen versus 1. FC Nürnberg
description_en:
On Sunday at 1:30 PM, Werder Bremen plays at home against Nuremberg. The organizer expects a full stadium.
Traffic disruptions, especially around the Weserstadion, are to be expected. The familiar traffic concept will be applied again. This means that the Osterdeich will be closed to individual traffic between Sielwall and Stader Straße approximately two and a half hours before and about one hour after the end of the game. Bremen Police therefore recommend that spectators arriving by vehicle use the offered Park+Ride service from Hemelinger Hafendamm.
Car break-ins repeatedly occur in the vicinity of football matches. Please do not leave any valuables in the vehicles. The stadium parking spaces are still only available to authorized persons with a corresponding parking permit.

title_en: Flight from the police ends in the median strip
description_en:
An 18-year-old driver evaded a police traffic stop in Gröpelingen on Tuesday afternoon. His escape ended in the verge. The adolescent did not possess a driver's license and had stolen license plates on the car.

The 18-year-old caught the attention of officers in Pastorenweg because he was not buckled up. The driver of the Alfa Romeo ignored the stop signals and instead floored it. He disregarded red lights and drove over tram tracks. To avoid endangering uninvolved parties, the police officers discontinued the pursuit. A short time later, the car was located again and stopped at the on-ramp to the A 281. A patrol car and the Alfa Romeo were damaged in the process. The driver ran out of the car, but was quickly apprehended and provisionally arrested. He now faces various criminal charges, such as endangering road traffic and driving without a license. Further investigations are ongoing.

On Friday evening, a seriously injured person in Huchting was reported to the Bremen police. A man was reportedly found at a bus stop with stab wounds. Witnesses discovered the 31-year-old man around 8 PM at the "Harriersand" bus stop on Huchtinger Heerstraße. He had multiple stab wounds on his body. The man was taken to a hospital for treatment. An immediate search for the perpetrators was unsuccessful. The 31-year-old was uncooperative towards the police officers. He provided no information about the exact crime scene nor about possible suspects.

title_en: Activists spray tanker on the Weser
description_en: On Monday afternoon, an oil tanker was sprayed with paint by activists while traveling on the Weser river near Bremen-Farge. The freighter was loaded with Russian oil and was on its way to the port of Bremen. Several people in three inflatable boats emblazoned the 200-meter-long tanker, which was sailing under the German flag, with the slogan "PEACE - NOT OIL". The water police of the Bremen police and support forces from Lower Saxony and Bremerhaven were on site with several boats and secured the area. Passing ship traffic was not impeded. The oil tanker was subsequently able to enter the industrial port in Bremen without further incidents. In the port basin there, additional people had gathered in smaller boats and six kayaks, displayed "Stop funding war" banners, and blocked the exit from the lock. The police repeatedly asked the group via loudspeaker announcement to name a meeting leader. No one identified themselves. A short time later, the gathering was dissolved by the police, and the activists were asked to leave the port basin. The individuals eventually complied. Recreational boats in the basin of an active industrial port are extremely dangerous, as large cargo ships can dock at any time, and are therefore prohibited. Police officers recorded the personal details of several individuals and filed corresponding reports for administrative offenses. The tanker is currently still accompanied by emergency forces on its way to its berth. Police measures and further investigations into possible criminal offenses are ongoing.

title_en: Public search after theft from jewelry store in Hamburg-Neustadt
description_en: With the help of the publication of several photos and videos, law enforcement authorities are now publicly searching for three currently unknown men and one woman. They are suspected of having jointly stolen high-value jewelry from a jewelry store in Hamburg city center at the beginning of December. For the original facts of the case, please refer to the previous press release, available at: https://www.presseportal.de/blaulicht/pm/6337/5924471. In the course of the investigations by LKA 115, indications have now emerged that the alleged gang of thieves could come from the Bremen area and have connections to North Rhine-Westphalia and Berlin. Since previous measures have not led to the identification of the quartet, a judge has now issued a warrant for public search at the request of the Hamburg public prosecutor's office.

title_en: Traffic jam, because truck did not retract its crane
description_en:
Yesterday afternoon, a 31-year-old truck driver was traveling on the Hemelingen motorway feeder road. Because his loading crane was not properly retracted, the crane collided with the sign gantry there, tore it down, and also damaged the roadway. Nobody was injured.

Around 1:50 PM, the truck driver was traveling with his vehicle from the Hemelingen Hafendamm in the direction of Motorway 1. For reasons currently unknown, the firmly mounted loading crane of the semi-trailer was not properly retracted, so the crane collided with the sign gantry there. Due to the impact, the crane tore off and fell onto the right lane, severely damaging both the crane itself, the asphalt, and the guardrail. For the duration of the cleanup work, the feeder road towards A1 had to be closed for about five hours, and operating fluids also leaked. This led to significant traffic obstructions. Traffic jams quickly formed on the alternative routes as well.

Property damage of almost 150,000 Euros occurred. For the asphalt repair work, the right lane is expected to remain closed until the end of the week. The traffic police department has commenced investigations.

title_en: Spaces still available: Talk "Sexualized Violence Online – Safely Guiding Children"
description_en: Children and young people today move quite naturally in the digital space - in chats, social networks, games and on video platforms. But where there are opportunities, risks also lurk. In this information event, we will first take a look at the digital world children live in: How digital is their everyday life? How much time do they spend online? What services do they use? Following this, we will address the dangers on the internet that children can be confronted with. The focus will be on the topics: Cybergrooming, pornographic content, sexting. In addition to understandable legal basics, participants will receive concrete behavioral and prevention tips for everyday life. Furthermore, it will be shown how adults should react when children come into contact with illegal content or boundary violations online. The event will be rounded off with information on support services and contact points that offer assistance to those affected and their caregivers.

title_en: Investigations into arson - Police arrest suspect
description_en:
Police officers apprehended a suspected arsonist in Vahr on Wednesday evening. The 41-year-old was provisionally arrested.

Witnesses observed a suspect setting fire to the tire of a car parked in Ferdinand-Lassalle-Straße. He then destroyed a side mirror with a kick and ripped off the handle of the Opel's driver's door. The fire did not spread to the entire vehicle and extinguished itself. A quickly arriving patrol was able to apprehend the suspect still nearby.

The police officers found a discarded lighter on the ground and secured it as evidence.

The 41-year-old suspect subsequently exhibited conspicuous psychological behavior and was, after an assessment, admitted to a psychiatric facility. Investigations into arson and criminal damage are ongoing.

In the district, several people clashed in front of a pub early on Sunday morning. A physical altercation ensued, including kicks to the head. A 17-year-old had to be admitted to a hospital. The police are looking for witnesses. A 33-year-old had initially gotten into an argument with several young men in a bar in the Steintor district. Outside the door, this escalated into a brawl. Initially, there were mutual blows. Subsequently, the 33-year-old was attacked by his opponents with fists and thrown bottles. When he then fell to the ground, the attackers also kicked him in the head. Only when witnesses intervened did the perpetrators cease their attack on their victim. The 33-year-old suffered minor injuries. Rapidly arriving emergency forces finally restored calm and provisionally arrested three suspects aged 17, 19, and 22. The 17-year-old then had to be taken to a hospital because he had significant lacerations on his body. It is currently being investigated how and where he sustained these injuries.

A 38-year-old man from Bremen got into an argument with two people at Bremen Central Station on Monday night into Tuesday and shot at the men with a gas pistol. An uninvolved woman was also injured during the altercation.

According to his own statements, the 38-year-old wanted to prevent his girlfriend from buying drugs from two men at the station square. During the argument, he shot at the presumed dealers with his gas pistol. The shooter also threw a bicycle in their direction, but hit a 20-year-old passerby, slightly injuring her. One of the two men complained of eye irritation and was taken to a hospital for outpatient treatment. The 38-year-old was provisionally arrested by the police. A blood sample was taken from the intoxicated man. He is now being investigated for grievous bodily harm and violations of the Weapons Act.

title_en: Who are the men from the supermarket?
description_en:
An incident on Monday evening with a suspected right-wing extremist background in a supermarket in Neustadt brought the State Security of the Bremen police into action. The investigators are also looking for an important customer.

Posts on the internet reported an incident in which, during the evening hours, a customer of a retail store in Bremen's Neustadt provoked other consumers with "extremely right-wing and racist symbols." When confronted about the symbols, this man reportedly pulled out a knife and pepper spray. After a discussion, he reportedly left the supermarket with a Hitler salute.

Investigations by the Bremen police quickly led to a supermarket on Gastfeldstraße. With the help of video recordings, the facts of the case could be further verified. According to current findings, an unknown man, who was carrying a backpack embroidered with a Confederate flag and right-wing extremist symbols, was approached by another customer. The unknown man then drew a knife, whereupon the other person stepped back. Both subsequently left the supermarket separately.

The identification of the suspect is ongoing.

title_en: World Cup in mind, street in sight
description_en: Goals, emotions, and an exuberant atmosphere are simply part of a Football World Cup. When there's cheering, spontaneous car parades in the Bremen city area are also not uncommon. The Bremen Police are happy about peaceful and joyful celebrations - but ask for compliance with some important rules. In short: Cheering is allowed - acrobatics on the car are not. Even during a car parade, the rules of the Road Traffic Act apply. Traffic lights remain red when they are red, seat belts must be worn, and a sufficient distance to the vehicle in front remains mandatory. Particularly important: Sitting or standing on vehicle roofs or bonnets, standing in vehicles - for example in convertibles -, leaning out of windows or sunroofs, as well as driving towards persons or groups of persons are dangerous and forbidden.

In a traffic accident on the night from Friday to Saturday in Sebaldsbrück, two people were seriously injured. The police are investigating and are looking for witnesses.Two 19-year-old men were driving their cars around 10:55 PM on Ludwig-Roselius-Allee in an outbound direction. One in his white BMW in the right lane, the other in his grey Daimler-Benz in the left lane, both, according to witness statements, at excessive speed. The driver of the BMW wanted to overtake a car in front of him, swerved to the left, and thereby collided with the Daimler driving next to him. Both drivers lost control, skidded, crashed into a tree which was torn down, and came to a stop in the oncoming lane. The driver of the BMW and his 18-year-old passenger were taken to a hospital with serious injuries. The other party involved in the accident and his 18-year-old occupant sustained minor injuries. The vehicles were a total write-off; they were impounded by the police for investigation.Further investigations by the traffic accident department, also due to a suspicion of participation in an illegal motor vehicle race on public roads, are ongoing.

title_en: Hazardous material spill in the container port
description_en: On Wednesday evening, there was a major operation by police and fire brigade at the container terminal in Bremerhaven. Shortly before 7 PM, the emergency services were alerted to an unusual smell in the container blocks along the Stromkaje. A patrol of the water police arrived first and cordoned off the area. The Bremerhaven fire brigade carried out measurements and subsequently discovered a leak in a tank container. The tank container contained a highly flammable liquid. Consequently, loading and unloading operations in the danger area were stopped. A 305-meter-long container ship had to be evacuated. Afterwards, the tank container was placed into a special container and transported to a hazardous goods area in the port. After the completion of the measures, the ship's crew was able to return to the container ship. The investigations by the water police of the Bremen police are ongoing.

On Thursday evening, a 39-year-old in Hemelingen injured his 37-year-old flatmate with a knife. A dispute is said to have preceded the attack. Around 8:45 PM, emergency services were called to Klinkkuhlenstraße; on-site, they heard voices and cries for help through a closed apartment door. After repeated requests, the door was finally opened, and the 37-year-old woman stepped into the hallway with a knife in her hand. The police then drew their firearms and ordered the woman to put down the knife. She only complied after the emergency services repeated the command multiple times. The woman had a stab wound on her leg. Inside the apartment, they encountered the 39-year-old flatmate of the woman, who was visibly under the influence of alcohol or drugs. He had scratches on his face and an injury to his ear. The 37-year-old was taken to a hospital by paramedics due to her stab wound, while the police took the 39-year-old to the station. There, he received an official police warning and an apartment exclusion order. Both accused each other of having attacked the other. A criminal complaint for grievous bodily harm was filed against the man, and a complaint for bodily harm was filed against his flatmate. Further investigations are ongoing.

Employees from the police, public order office, and trade office inspected several arcades and restaurants in Blumenthal on Wednesday afternoon. They found only a few violations.
The inspections focused on compliance with youth protection, the Corona ordinance, and trade regulations. A total of seven establishments were checked between 4:00 PM and 8:00 PM. Among other things, the employees found violations of the Corona ordinance and the Closed Substance Cycle and Waste Management Act. In one case, there is a suspicion of accepting illegal bets. None of the violations led to the closure of arcades or restaurants. The employees of the public order office have already set dates for follow-up inspections with the operators. In the future, the police will also carry out such inspections in restaurants and arcades to verify compliance with legal requirements.

title_en: Of flying wallets and repentant robbers
description_en: A duo of robbers mugged a 26-year-old passerby in Bremen-Mitte on Sunday night. When he was no longer responsive, the men showed remorse and administered first aid. Their subsequent fabricated alibi quickly collapsed. The two 18 and 19-year-old adolescents, one in acute financial distress, the other out on probation, approached the 26-year-old man on Am Wall street and knocked him down. They stole his wallet and smartphone and then wanted to flee. However, since the victim was temporarily unconscious, they turned back and placed him in the recovery position. They then called emergency services and presented themselves to the paramedics as helpful witnesses. When the also alerted police officers discovered the 26-year-old's wallet in the 19-year-old's jacket pocket, and the latter could not explain it at all, the invented helper story collapsed like a house of cards. Handcuffs clicked for the adolescents; they were provisionally arrested. An ambulance took the 26-year-old, now conscious again, to a hospital for outpatient treatment.

On Wednesday, a 30-year-old in Westend attempted to rob two men of cigarettes. He hit them and threatened them with a blank-firing pistol. Emergency services located the suspect and provisionally arrested him.

Around 6:50 AM, a 36-year-old and a 23-year-old were in Gustavstraße when an unknown person asked them for cigarettes. When they explained they were non-smokers, he kicked and punched the 36-year-old man. The two fought back and pushed him, whereupon the assailant pulled a firearm from his jacket. The 23-year-old stated that the unknown person aimed the weapon at him and pulled the trigger. He heard a click, like an unloaded weapon. The men struggled with him again, after which he fled. The two called 110 and provided a description of the perpetrator. They were slightly injured in the incident.

Shortly after, a witness contacted the police and stated that he had also seen a man handling a firearm. Subsequently, police officers heard loud shouts near the station. A man was standing on the street who matched the witnesses' description and admitted to the emergency services that he had "done something foolish." They took him to the station, where he was searched and had his identity established. They could not find a weapon on the 30-year-old. A voluntary breath alcohol test revealed a value of more than 1.6 per mille. In the course of further investigations, a female witness came forward. She handed over a firearm to the emergency services, which she had found on Helgolander Straße. The weapon was confiscated. Police officers filed a criminal complaint for attempted robbery. The investigations are ongoing.

An armed robber attacked a gas station in Kirchhuchting on Sunday evening. The masked man stole cash and fled undetected. Around 9 PM, the man entered the salesroom of the gas station on Kirchhuchtinger Landstraße. He threatened the 25-year-old employee with a firearm and took cash from the register. Afterwards, he fled with the loot on a bicycle in the direction of Moordeicher Landstraße. The robber was described as being about 25 years old and 180 centimeters tall. He wore a black hooded jacket and dark Adidas brand jogging pants with white stripes. Furthermore, the man was equipped with sunglasses with a blue mirror finish.

As part of a targeted operation in the parking garages around the main train station, plainclothes officers of the Bremen police apprehended a 33-year-old drug dealer on early Tuesday evening. He had threatened two men with a knife after a drug deal.In recent weeks, car break-ins and drug-related crime had repeatedly occurred in the parking garages in the Mitte district. The police reacted with increased presence and focused controls.Plainclothes officers were in a parking garage in Rembertiring around 6:45 PM when three men stormed into the parking garage. One of the three held a knife over his head and shouted something at the other two men. The police identified themselves and loudly ordered the 33-year-old, with drawn firearms, to drop the knife. He only complied after the officers repeated this several times.The 33-year-old man was provisionally arrested and taken to a police station. During a search, the police found further drugs. Investigations, including for attempted grievous bodily harm, are ongoing.

The Bremen Police, together with the Public Order Office, customs, the tax office, the Bremen fire department, and employees of the food inspection authority, carried out checks on Monday in the districts of Mitte, Walle, Gröpelingen, and Neustadt. Restaurants, snack bars, and shisha bars were inspected, and a multitude of deficiencies were found. A shisha bar had to be temporarily evacuated due to excessively high CO levels. In addition, a restaurant in the Bahnhofsvorstadt (station district) was closed. In the respective districts, a total of 13 establishments were the focus of the emergency services from afternoon until the evening hours. In all inspected premises, the forces found various violations, such as massive cash register deficiencies, violations of the Weapons Act, labeling requirements, and the Packaging Act, youth violations, and hygiene deficiencies. Corresponding reports were filed. Employees of the Public Order Office closed a restaurant in the Bahnhofsvorstadt due to a multitude of violations, including hygienic deficiencies and improper food storage. In Neustadt, a blackjack was found in a shisha bar. A corresponding criminal complaint was filed. Fire department emergency services also had to temporarily evacuate another shisha bar in Neustadt because the CO level was too high. No one was injured. For many weeks and months, the Bremen Police have been increasingly committed to combating street crime and will continue these efforts together with other security authorities.

On the night from Tuesday to Wednesday, officers from the traffic enforcement unit conducted speed checks in Walle. Significant speed violations were detected. Drivers face potentially severe fines and driving bans. In total, 40 vehicles were measured on Bremerhavener Straße. In an area with a 50 km/h speed limit, the fastest car was measured at 107 km/h. In less than two hours, six drivers were caught who now face driving bans and high fines. The Bremen Police will continue to conduct targeted traffic checks, both stationary and mobile, using patrol cars or unmarked vehicles.

title_en: Drunk man crashes into car, bicycles and a house wall
description_en: Early Saturday morning, a drunk 21-year-old in Bremen Mitte lost control of his Mercedes and crashed into a house wall after also hitting several bicycles and a car. Around 4:45 AM, a patrol car crew saw the damaged Mercedes standing in Abbentorswallstraße. When they spoke to the 21-year-old sitting inside, they noticed he smelled of alcohol. He had apparently first veered off the road to the right and collided with several bicycles and a tree. After that, he continued to swerve and hit a concrete staircase and the house wall, and finally a parked car on the other side of the street. A breath alcohol test showed almost 1.5 per mille, and the 21-year-old also admitted to having consumed marijuana. The police took him to the station, which apparently made him feel mistreated, because there he started to rampage. After he had hit several panes of glass, he was placed in a detention cell. His minor injuries were treated by the emergency services called to the scene. The police filed a report against the 21-year-old for endangering road traffic. He also now faces a driving ban. The accident resulted in estimated property damage of more than 20,000 Euros.

title_en: New Year's Eve in the Hanseatic City - Bremen Police draws preliminary balance
description_en:
The Bremen police had a busy night. On New Year's Eve, many typical offenses such as assaults, improper handling of fireworks, and violations of the Explosives Act kept the emergency services busy. In addition, there were isolated attacks on police and fire department emergency services again, including with pyrotechnics. Five police officers sustained acoustic trauma, but were able to continue their duty. The fire department had to be supported during operations after emergency services had been attacked. According to current information, no equipment was damaged.

This year too, the police were deployed in the city with increased forces. The police officers responded to 300 incidents between 6 PM and 6 AM on New Year's morning.

Numerous people celebrated the turn of the year on the streets of Bremen, especially around the station forecourt, the Schlachte, the Weser bridges, and the Sielwall intersection. New Year's Eve fireworks were extensively set off everywhere. The police had an increased presence at the hotspots and primarily punished violations of the firecracker ban. In addition, between midnight and 1 AM, there were several fires in the city area, including various apartment and dumpster fires as well as two vehicle fires.

At the Sielwall intersection, waste paper, rubbish, and an e-scooter were repeatedly set on fire. Suspects were apprehended by the police. During the arrest, there were acts of solidarity and the emergency services were attacked. They had to use irritant gas to calm the situation. Due to being pelted with objects and attacked with firecrackers, the fire department could not enter the area. The small fire was therefore extinguished by the police's water cannon. Nobody was injured. Investigations into this are ongoing.

"Five States - One Goal - Safety on Recreational Boats" – under this heading, joint recreational boat inspection days took place for the first time, involving the water police authorities of the states of Lower Saxony, Bremen, Hamburg, Schleswig-Holstein, and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. The inspection days were prepared and conceived by the State Water Police Office of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. During generally calm public holidays, the deployed officers observed various infringements of maritime shipping and traffic law regulations. The participating officers from the police stations in the coastal states inspected 559 recreational boats, watercraft, and watersports enthusiasts, particularly on Ascension Day and Whit Monday. Among the inspected watercraft were 554 vessels flying the German flag and five from other EU member states. The water police recorded 69 violations. Two criminal offenses and 13 administrative offenses related to maritime policing were recorded. Furthermore, there were nine cases of alcohol-related impairment of the skipper while operating their vessel. In three of these cases, further travel had to be prohibited, as the consumption of alcohol was deemed to pose a danger to other waterway users. 32 violations of regional navigation regulations of the coastal states were sanctioned, as well as eight violations of the Recreational Boating License Ordinance (Sea). In Bremen, the water police of the Bremen Police inspected over 30 recreational boats during these days and identified and sanctioned 15 violations, including fishing in the fairway, entering harbors, speeding violations, and equipment violations.

A 31-year-old man robbed an arcade in Neustadt on the night of Wednesday to Thursday, injuring a 45-year-old employee. The police were able to arrest the robber while he was fleeing. The 31-year-old entered the arcade on Friedrich-Ebert-Straße, walked directly to the counter and demanded cash from the employee. He kept his hands in his jacket pockets, feigning a dangerous object. He then grabbed the woman by her hair and pushed her down. The 45-year-old grabbed her pepper spray and used it against the attacker. He then fled without any loot. Rapidly arriving emergency services apprehended him near the crime scene. Both individuals were slightly injured by inhaling the irritant gas and had to be treated. The robber was subsequently admitted to a psychiatric hospital.

After a robber armed with a knife attacked a kiosk in Oslebshausen on Monday evening, the police arrested the suspected perpetrator. Reasons for his detention are currently being examined for the 25-year-old.

Around 10:50 PM, the man entered the kiosk on Oslebshauser Heerstraße. The alleged customer placed a pack of cigarettes on the sales counter. When the employee then opened the cash register, he immediately threatened him with a knife and reached into the cash register himself. He then fled the store, but was caught by the employee and held until the arrival of alerted emergency forces.

The 25-year-old from Bremen was arrested and processed for identification. He is to be brought before a detention judge today. Investigations against him for aggravated robbery are ongoing.

An unknown perpetrator robbed a liquor store in Mitte on Tuesday evening. He threatened the 19-year-old employee with a knife, stole cash, and fled. The police are looking for witnesses. At 6:25 PM, the man entered the salesroom on Schwachhauser Heerstraße. He first took a bottle from a shelf and went to the checkout. When the 19-year-old asked him to pay, the robber pulled out a knife and demanded in English that she hand over money. The employee then handed over cash. Subsequently, the man fled with the cash and a bottle of whiskey in the direction of Hollerallee. The perpetrator was described as follows: He was approximately 180 to 190 cm tall and about 30 to 40 years old. He was wearing a dark jacket, grey trousers, a plaid shirt, and black shoes with white soles. On his head, he wore a red-white-green striped wool hat.

A young robber attacked a gas station in Walle early Tuesday morning. The police were able to arrest the suspected perpetrator on the same day after intensive follow-up investigations. He is suspected of having robbed this gas station for the third time already (see press releases No. 0650 and 0035). Currently, grounds for detention are being examined against the 18-year-old.
Early Tuesday, the young man entered the salesroom of the gas station on Hans-Böckler-Straße, threatened an employee with a blank-firing pistol and demanded cash. When the woman explained that she had hardly any money in the till, the perpetrator became nervous and fled the store without any loot. During this, a shot was accidentally fired. Nobody was injured.
Through the evaluation of video footage and witness statements, the 18-year-old came into the focus of the investigators. The suspect was arrested in his apartment by special forces. According to the current state of investigations, he is responsible for two further robberies at the same gas station.
He is to be brought before a remand judge today. Further investigations are ongoing.

In the early hours of Sunday morning, unknown individuals broke into a post office branch in the Oslebshausen district. The owner of the post office branch on Schragerstraße contacted the police around 5 AM on Sunday morning and reported that his branch had been broken into. According to initial findings, the unknown persons climbed onto the roof of an adjacent shopping center using a ladder and gained access to the post office branch through a window opening that they forcibly opened. The burglars searched the premises, rummaged through several cabinets, and stole two empty cash deposit boxes, which they left behind on the roof during their escape.

Unknown perpetrators extensively defaced a noise barrier in Gröpelingen between Friday and Monday. The police are looking for witnesses. On Monday around 09:30 AM, employees of the BSAG discovered the graffiti in Basdahler Straße. Among other things, the unknown individuals had sprayed "ACAB" and other slogans with different colors over a length of approximately 60 meters. The criminal police have started investigations and are looking for witnesses.

Unknown individuals presumably defaced a party office in Vegesack with paint overnight into Tuesday. The police are looking for witnesses. The perpetrators pelted the facade of the CDU office with a white paint bomb and extensively sprayed the word "Filth" in yellow paint onto the entrance door. The police have opened an investigation into criminal damage.

Bremen Police achieve quick investigative success. After a young person was kicked unconscious by an assailant in Vegesack on Tuesday evening (see also press release 566), emergency responders provisionally arrested the suspected perpetrator on Wednesday morning. The 14-year-old boy was kicked unconscious by the assailant on Tuesday evening in Gerhard-Rohlfs-Straße. When a passer-by intervened, the violent offender fled. Criminal police investigations quickly led to a 15-year-old from Vegesack. He was arrested on Wednesday morning. During the search of the apartment, the police officers secured evidence. After the completion of police measures, the 15-year-old was handed over to his father. According to the current state of investigations, the 14-year-old boy was initially held by four to five young people on Tuesday evening. A previously unknown individual from this group snatched his bag, and subsequently, the 15-year-old then punched and kicked him. Investigations into the accomplices are ongoing.

Unknown persons manipulated the water pumps in a shell building in Oberneuland on the night from Tuesday to Wednesday, causing considerable damage. The criminal police are looking for witnesses.The intruders dismantled the pumps of the large construction site in Louis-Leitz-Straße, so that water could no longer drain away. In addition, the unknown persons deactivated the electrical circuit. As a result of these actions, the groundwater rose by almost half a meter overnight. The exact damage cannot yet be precisely quantified, but amounts to at least a five-figure sum.The criminal police are investigating for causing a flood. "Whoever causes a flood and thereby endangers property of significant value belonging to another shall be punished with imprisonment from one year to ten years."

On Tuesday afternoon, several masked individuals gained access to a house in Horn. The police were on site with strong forces. The operation was concluded in the evening.

Around 2:45 PM, witnesses reported via emergency call that the group had entered the property on Horner Heerstraße with a ladder and camping equipment. At the same time, a group classified as left-wing extremist by the Office for the Protection of the Constitution, calling itself "rosarote Zora," published pictures on social media and claimed responsibility for the action. The pictures showed people on the balcony of the house with banners. Inscriptions such as "ACAT" and "Bomb away the patriarchy" were written on them. The police quickly arrived with operational forces, who saw several activists on the property and cordoned off the area. The owner had in the meantime filed a criminal complaint and pointed out that the house was very dilapidated.

The operational forces entered the property, addressed the individuals, and requested them to leave. Subsequently, the operational forces escorted twelve people from the property and established their identities. Criminal charges were filed for trespassing, and eviction orders were issued. The fire department supported the police during the subsequent inspection and securing of the building. No persons were found in the house by the operational forces, but mattresses and provisions were discovered. The banners hung on the house were removed by operational forces. In the evening, the house was handed over to a representative of the owner. In the course of the afternoon, about 20 people gathered on the opposite side of the street and held a spontaneous demonstration.

A 39-year-old smeared a police patrol car with anti-police slogans on Thursday evening in Bremen-Mitte. As part of an operation, the officers went into Bremen Central Station. They parked the patrol car in front of the main entrance. When they returned to the vehicle after completing the operation, passers-by spoke to the officers. An unknown person had smeared their police car. The witnesses identified the perpetrator, who was currently heading towards the side entrance of the station. The officers apprehended the 39-year-old, who immediately confessed to the act. "It would have been a stupid idea," the heavily intoxicated man recognized in a moment of clarity. Nevertheless, the officers took the artistically inclined man to the station. He was subsequently released after the completion of police measures.

In the night from Sunday to Monday, burglars broke into a bakery in Schwachhausen. Among other things, the thieves attempted to steal a safe and fled undetected. The police are looking for witnesses. First, the burglars smashed the window pane of the bakery branch on Georg-Grüning-Straße. Subsequently, the intruders searched all cupboards and drawers in the salesroom and stole a metal cash box. From another room, a safe was moved to the window, ready for collection. Meanwhile, attentive residents had alerted the police via emergency call, whereupon two perpetrators fled from the shop in the direction of Hollerallee. The duo was described with dark clothing and black masks. An immediate search initiated for the suspects was unsuccessful. The criminal police have taken up the investigation and are looking for further witnesses to the crime.

title_en: Another arrest warrant for street robber
description_en:
Police forces from Bremen apprehended a 43-year-old in the city center on Wednesday morning. A man had recognized him as a robber.

Around 11:10 AM, the police officers were called to Sögestraße. On site, in front of a shop, they encountered the 43-year-old and a 41-year-old. The latter stated that he had been in the vicinity of the main train station in the early morning hours. There, this man had pulled his mobile phone out of his pocket. Subsequently, an unknown person had threatened him with a knife and demanded cash. After he had handed over the money, he was injured on the hand by the unknown person with the knife. He had reported the robbery at a federal police station; an immediately initiated search had been unsuccessful.

The officers took the man from Morocco, who was heavily under the influence of drugs, to the station. The Bremen public prosecutor's office obtained an arrest warrant due to a multitude of similar offenses, and he was transferred to a correctional facility. Investigations concerning the second man are ongoing.
